text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY

- Russian investment bank ICFI, a unit of Uneximbank-MFK financial group, and investment bank Renaissance Capital are merging to form a new investment bank to compete equally with similar Western financial bodies.
- A government commission will be set up to monitor oil exports under share productions agreements.
- Russia is imposing customs duties on most of the products brought in from Belarus.
- The Central Bank of Russia has introduced new rules to help commercial banks fight money-laundering.
- Russia's biggest car makers, Moskvich and Avtovaz, are planning to launch joint production of a new medium-sized car.
- Commander of Russia's interior troops, Anatoly Shkirko, a strong supporter of using force against Chechnya, has offered his resignation.
SEVODNAY
- A tender on Cuban sugar in exchange for Russian oil is to take place by the end of summer.
- The government is planning to change customs dutied for alumina imports.

- Oil exporting companies are expected to raise Western credits more easily after scrapping quotas for exports of crude oil under so-called federal programmes, says Deputy Energy and Fuel Minister Sergei Kiriyenko.

- Indonesia's research and technology minister seems to have reached agreement with Russian officials on a deal totalling one billion dollars, says the paper. Indonesia is known to be interested in Russia's SU-30 fighters.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Russia's Prosecutor General has recommended that President Boris Yeltsin cancel the auction of Tyumen Oil Company shares.
- The government expects 5 percent inflation for the next year, says First Deputy Finance Aleksei Kudrin.
- Moscow Stock Exchange will start trading operations with gold next week.
- Kuzbass coal miners, the biggest coal region in Siberia, have resumed their protest calling on the government and the president to resign.
IZVESTIA
- Unified Energy Systems is planning to float bonds totalling about five trillion roubles, said First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov.
- Russian investment bank ICFI, a unit of the Uneximbank-MFK financial group, and investment bank Renaissance Capital are merging to form a new investment bank with total assets of over $2 billion.
- Russia will pay off at least 4.2 trillion roubles in wage arrears to the military by the end of the year.
- While the Russian space crew fights problems at the troubled Mir station, mission control officials are keeping them in the dark about their families, the paper says.
ROSSIISKAYA GAZETA
- The government is planning to bring forward the launch in Russia of the world system of urgent communication during sea accidents.
- A new concept for developing Russian aviation is under consideration by the government, says Yevgeny Shaposhnikov, the president's aide on aviation.
ROSSISKIYE VESTI
- Boris Yeltsin has signed a decree scrapping quotas for government-sponsored exports of crude oil under so-called federal programmes.
- Russia has set a deadline for paying off massive wage arrears to the military and public sector workers.
- NATO has opened its doors in order to be closer to Russia's frontiers, says the paper, commenting on the results of the NATO summit in Madrid.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS

- The head of the investment bank Renaissance Capital, Boris Yordan, is likely to become head of the new super investment bank set up after the merger of Renaissance Capital with ICFI investment bank, says the paper.
--Tatyana Ustinova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
